title: Half of a two-tailed significance level, as a percentage
source: S2 Ch1 theory S2-1.2 Quick check 1 (10% two-tailed test, each tail compared with 5%)
stem: A two-tailed test is carried out at the {a|int}\% significance level, with the significance level shared equally between the two tails. With what percentage is each tail probability compared?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: Each tail is compared with half of the significance level, \(\dfrac{{a|int}}{2}\%\).

contexts.stem: In a two-tailed test at the {a|int}\% level the significance level is shared equally. What percentage is used as the threshold in each tail?
A two-tailed hypothesis test uses a {a|int}\% significance level, split equally between the two critical regions. With what percentage should an observed tail probability be compared?

title: Lower tail P(X is at most 1) for a binomial distribution
source: S2 Ch1 theory S2-1.2 Quick check 2 (B(8,0.25), P(X<=1)=0.367 to 3 s.f.)
stem: Given that \(X\sim\mathrm{B}({n|int},\,{p|raw})\), find \(\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 1)\), correct to 3 significant figures.

steps.name: form
steps.note: Write the two binomial terms for a short lower tail.

steps.name: E
steps.text_tex: The value is \({E|sf3z}\) to 3 significant figures.

contexts.stem: A trial is repeated independently {n|int} times, and the probability of success on each trial is {p|raw}. If \(X\) is the number of successes, find \(\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant 1)\), correct to 3 significant figures.

A sample of {n|int} packets is inspected. The probability that a packet is a special edition is {p|raw}, independently of the others. Find the probability that at most one packet is a special edition, correct to 3 significant figures.

title: Expected number of successes under H0 for a binomial sample
source: S2 Ch1 theory S2-1.2 Quick check 3 (B(20,0.4), mean np=8)
stem: Under \(H_0\) a random variable has the distribution \(\mathrm{B}({n|int},\,{p|raw})\). What is the expected number of successes in the {n|int} trials?

contexts.stem: A two-tailed test uses the null hypothesis that \(X\sim\mathrm{B}({n|int},\,{p|raw})\). Find the expected number of successes under \(H_0\).
A random sample of {n|int} trials is modelled, under \(H_0\), by a binomial distribution with success probability {p|raw}. What is the expected number of successes?
